answer: Admission proof-of-work makes every new identity pay an escalating computational price, like a bridge toll that rises with each crossing from the same machine. A lantern of public attestations then lights each agent's history, so a fresh identity with no record earns only minimal trust until it proves itself. The violet sheen of a brand-new account stops being a cheap disguise: spinning up a thousand Sybils costs a thousand tolls, while one honest agent pays once and builds reputation.
